title: Regional drain misconfiguration triggered misroutes and cascading model fallbacks — incident postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-14 an automated region drain job incorrectly marked a healthy region (eu-west-1) as draining. The smart routing controller treated the region as unavailable and re-routed traffic through tier-based policies which pushed load to lower-cost (cpu-quantized) model variants and remote regions. This produced a cascading series of capacity constraints and fallbacks that caused elevated latency and 5xx errors for a subset of premium customers for ~2 hours.

This ticket contains the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and required follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-14T09:02:12Z - Automated drain job (drain-controller v2.3) executed as scheduled for maintenance window.
2026-02-14T09:02:23Z - drain-controller incorrectly applied 'state: draining' to eu-west-1 control-plane due to a mismatched region alias in the maintenance config.
2026-02-14T09:03:05Z - Smart routing service observed eu-west-1 as 'unavailable' and began re-routing based on policy: prefer same-region -> dedicated pool -> fallback tier -> remote-region.
2026-02-14T09:04:00Z - Traffic to eu-west-1 shifted to remote region us-east-1 and to lower-tier model variants (cpu-quantized), increasing token-latency and CPU contention.
2026-02-14T09:10:00Z - Error rate spike observed on premium routes: 5xx rate rose from 0.3% to 11.7%; median latency increased from 95ms to 540ms for affected customers.
2026-02-14T09:20:00Z - Oncall notified (pager) and incident commander (IC) assigned. Initial mitigation: pause automated drain job and force eu-west-1 to healthy in service registry.

2026-02-14T09:35:00Z - Partial traffic restored to eu-west-1, but model variant churn continued due to warmed KV cache loss and prefix cache misses leading to transient latency and token cost increase.
2026-02-14T11:15:00Z - SLOs restored to normal; incident declared resolved after monitoring window with no reoccurrence.
2026-02-14T11:40:00Z - Post-incident bridge created for deeper analysis (this document).
root_cause: A maintenance config used an outdated region alias ("eu-w-1") which matched a pattern in the drain-controller's alias resolver. The controller's safety checks allowed a positive match and set 'state: draining' for the eu-west-1 control-plane. The smart routing controller treated the control-plane state as region unavailable without cross-checking node-level health or tier capacity. Combined with routing policy priorities that favored remote regions and degraded model variants, the system created a feedback loop: increased latency -> more fallbacks -> capacity oversubscription in remote pools.
impact_summary: Duration: ~2h13m; Affected customers: ~82 premium customers using regional pinning in EU; Peak 5xx rate: 11.7%; Median latency impact: +445ms for affected traffic; Billing/units: token cost increased ~18% for impacted calls due to longer tails and model variant changes.
immediate_mitigations: Paused scheduled drains and rolled drain-controller back to v2.2 within 10 minutes of detection.
Manually set eu-west-1 region state to 'healthy' in service registry and triggered an explicit routing refresh.
Opened an elevated autoscale window for dedicated pools in us-east-1 to reduce contention while traffic rebalanced.
Enabled temporary stricter fallback thresholds to prevent switching to lower-tier variants unless latency > 1s for > 30s.
long_term_actions: (A1) Add a two-way validation in drain-controller: require both region-alias exact match and at least one node-level health signal before marking draining. Owner: Marco Chen. ETA: 2026-03-05.

(A2) Modify smart routing controller to consult node readiness and warm-cache indicators (KV cache age, prefix-hit ratio) before triggering cross-region routing. Owner: Reliability team. ETA: 2026-03-12.
(A3) Introduce a circuit-breaker for cascading fallbacks: limit concurrent fallback rate per tenant and per route to 5% of baseline QPS. Owner: Serving runtime. ETA: 2026-03-19.
(A4) Rigorous integration test for maintenance workflows: simulate drain + routing decision under load in staging. Owner: SRE/Test infra. ETA: 2026-03-01.
(A5) Update runbook and oncall playbook with explicit steps to forcibly rebind region pins and how to revert drain-controller states. Owner: Oncall docs. ETA: 2026-02-27.
(A6) Post-incident review with product teams to revisit routing priority defaults for premium customers (consider 'honor-region-pin' hard guard). Owner: PM - Nina Verma. ETA: 2026-03-08.
action_items: ENG-5315: Implement alias-resolver exact-match guard in drain-controller (assignee: Marco Chen) - 5 pts
ENG-5316: Extend smart-routing health checks to include node readiness and cache state (assignee: Priya Rao) - 8 pts
ENG-5317: Add fallback circuit-breaker and rate limiter per-tenant (assignee: Luis Morales) - 8 pts
DOC-119: Update maintenance runbook with forced-unwind steps and verification checklist (assignee: Rachel Lowe) - 3 pts
OPS-78: Create staging chaos test that simulates region drain under load (assignee: SRE) - 5 pts
